newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Strike paralyzes Argentine grain port Necochea.
newsitem.headline: Strike paralyzes Argentine grain port Necochea.

text.p: Necochea, one of Argentina's main grains ports, was paralyzed Thursday by a general strike called by opposition unions, shipping agents said.

Officials at the NABSA shipping agency reported that Necochea, a major port in southern Buenos Aires province, was completely closed by the strike. They said that some terminals in the port of San Lorenzo were also closed.
Security officials contacted by Reuters at Necochea confirmed other workers were absent.
They added that there were no ships in the port of Bahia Blanca, so whether it was working or not had little importance. They were not sure if Buenos Aires was working.
But National Port Administration officials reported that the port of Buenos Aires appeared to be working normally.
The CTA and MTA opposition unions called a general strike to protest against unemployment and proposed government labor market reforms.

The pro-government CGT, the country's largest union federation, has reached a deal with the government on labor market reforms and opposes the strike. But its political arm, the "62 Peronist Organizations," supports the stoppage.
This will be the fourth general strike in just over a year against President Carlos Menem's Peronist government. The previous strikes were organized by the CGT.
